newsitem.title: USA: Millennium Pharm says issued patent.
newsitem.headline: Millennium Pharm says issued patent.

text.p: Millennium Pharmaceuticals Inc said Tuesday the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office has issued a patent for its novel melanoma gene.
The company said the gene, fomy030, encodes a protein called melastatin that functions as a metastasis suppressor in malignant melanoma.
Melanoma is a type of skin cancer with an estimated 40,000 new cases diagnosed each year.

Frank Lee, Millennium's Chief Scientific Officer, said, "We found that the presence of the protein melastatin inhibits the metastasis phenotype, and that the absence of the protein, resulting for example from a mutation in the fomy030 gene, can cause cancerous skin cells to metastasize."

"We are pleased with the broad scope of this patent as it covers fomy030 gene sequences and other closely related genes that inhibit tumor progression or metastatic disease," said Mark Boshar, Millennium's Chief Patent Officer.

In addition, Boshar added, "we have received notices of allowances from the U.S. Patent Office for other patent applications covering disease genes, including further patent applications related to fomy030."
Millennium employs large-scale genetics, genomics, high-throughput screening and bioinformatics in an integrated, broad-based drug discovery program applicable to all major human diseases.
